subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI cross-channel observe/mirror mode, and what authorization, disclosure, session-scope, and delivery semantics should it enforce?
rationale: The source gap is real, but implementing it changes channel/session visibility and likely adds public CLI or config surface, so automation cannot choose the safe product boundary.

options.title: Design guarded observe mode
options.body: Add a default-off read-only observer first, with explicit operator auth, bounded/redacted display, no outbound channel delivery, docs, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Only land selected-session live updates
options.body: Treat the open TUI live-update PR as the supported fix and leave broad all-channel mirroring out of scope for now.

options.title: Keep logs and Control UI as observer surfaces
options.body: Document openclaw logs --follow and existing UI activity surfaces as the intended monitoring path instead of adding cross-channel visibility to TUI.

recommendation.title: Design guarded observe mode
recommendation.body: Add a default-off read-only observer first, with explicit operator auth, bounded/redacted display, no outbound channel delivery, docs, tests, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This crosses TUI UX, session-state, channel visibility, and security defaults, and steipete has the strongest adjacent ownership signal from the active PR and merged history.
